mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-rate periods (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS acceleration and SPX 60-day returns in out-of-sample tests (R² < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% suggests resilient demand, which anticipates a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market participants price in future earnings growth.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL monthly acceleration (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -1% indicates weakening supply-side conditions, which typically precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate soft landing difficulties.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains flat or expands in subsequent months without SPX underperforming (down >5%) in 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, it triggers a regime shift to monetary easing, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns in the current easing cycle.
failure_condition: Crossing not followed by statistically significant positive 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tight labor market, which can drive positive 60-day S&P 500 returns through optimism about future hiring.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months while UNRATE remains below 4%
failure_condition: No significant positive returns in out-of-sample periods with similar labor conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly retail sales (not available in provided series - use alternative supply proxy: GDPC1 as industrial production proxy) below -2% for two months suggests softening demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the softening period.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for four consecutive months, it signals a high-interest environment that discourages risk-taking, typically resulting in negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays above 5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the high-rate period.
